acceptable_forms_in_preference_order.note: Strongest. A question set over the ASM collections with reference answers and, ideally, the doc_id or chunk_id values that jointly contain each answer. Verdicts become mechanical and the leaderboard is trustworthy. For synthesis questions the key must name the SET of required source documents, not a single one.

acceptable_forms_in_preference_order.gold_object: For each question: a gold EVIDENCE SET -- two or more chunk_ids drawn from two or more DISTINCT doc_ids within one collection -- plus an enumerated list of the required evidence items the answer must contain, one per contributing document.
acceptable_forms_in_preference_order.note: The declared fallback and the expected path. Revised from the single-chunk form to match the operator's synthesis weighting. Instead of sampling one chunk and asking a question it answers, identify a pivot shared by several documents in a collection and generate a question that cannot be answered correctly from any one of them alone.
acceptable_forms_in_preference_order.why_acceptable: Grounded in the corpus rather than in a model's opinion, and it makes the two measures that matter mechanically computable: document coverage (how many of the required distinct documents were retrieved) and synthesis completeness (how many of the required evidence items the answer actually states).

acceptable_forms_in_preference_order.note: Weakest and must be declared as such if used. A model judging its own pipeline's output measures self-consistency, not correctness, and a configuration that is confidently wrong scores well. Additionally unreliable for synthesis specifically: a fluent answer built from two of three required papers reads as complete to a judge that has not been told what the third paper contributes.
acceptable_forms_in_preference_order.permitted_only_if: the run declares itself a self-assessment study and never presents its output as a correctness ranking

construction_method_for_rank_2.per_collection: Constructed independently within each collection. A question must never require evidence from a document in a different collection, because no trial ever retrieves across collections.
pivot_discovery: Preferred where the graph is available for the collection: GET /v1/graph/entities returns entities most-connected first; GET /v1/graph/neighbors/{entity} returns triples each carrying a chunk_id, so a pivot entity whose triples resolve to two or more distinct doc_ids is a ready-made cross-paper link.

Fallback where the graph is unavailable or empty for that collection: issue a broad POST /v1/retrieve at high top_k on a topical probe, group returned chunks by doc_id, and keep pivots whose top-scoring chunks span two or more documents.
construction_method_for_rank_2.validation: Every generated question must be checked against its own gold evidence set before the set is frozen: the question must be unanswerable from any single contributing document alone. A question that one document answers on its own is a lookup question, not a synthesis question, and belongs in the control class.

benchmark_requirement.freeze_rule: The question set, its gold evidence sets, and the required-evidence-item lists are frozen before the first scored trial and are not edited afterward. A benchmark edited mid-run invalidates every comparison made across the edit.

mix.control_class_why: Single-document lookup questions are retained as a control arm, not as the main event. They are what makes a claim about bm25 versus vector interpretable, and they are the reference against which the synthesis penalty of any configuration is measured.
mix.ruling: Operator directive: 'preferable multi-paper synthesis'. The benchmark is weighted toward questions that require integrating evidence from two or more distinct documents WITHIN one collection.

collection_strata.aggregation_across_collections: Reporting only, never scoring. A cross-collection summary may note that an axis moved the same direction everywhere, or that it did not. It must never average scores across collections into a single headline number, because collections differ in size, chunk strategy and graph availability, and an average would hide exactly the variation this study exists to surface.
collection_strata.definition: Each readable ASM collection enumerated by GET /v1/collections is an independent experimental stratum with its own benchmark question set, its own trial leaderboard, its own winning configuration profile, and its own findings.
collection_strata.no_union_arm: The multi-collection union is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE. No trial may pass a `collections` array with more than one element. Every request names exactly one collection explicitly.
collection_strata.ruling: Operator directive: collections are used and measured SEPARATELY, not merged.
collection_strata.why_it_matters: A per-collection design costs more calls than a union design and buys the ability to say that an axis helped one collection and hurt another. A union design cannot say that, and the operator has ruled that distinction in.

per_collection_outputs: winning configuration profile, as a runnable JSON object naming every parameter and the episode structure
trial leaderboard, one row per trial, carrying the full parameter vector, the score, the document-coverage measure, the synthesis-completeness measure, and the cost vector
per-question outcome rows for every trial: returned answer, cited doc_ids and chunk_ids, distinct-document count, verdict, failure class where wrong, truncated flag
the frozen benchmark question set with its gold evidence sets
findings note: which axes mattered in THIS collection, which did not, which could not be tested and why
run_level_outputs: the resolved QueryRequest schema as fetched, with fetch timestamp
the collection, prompt-template and model inventories as fetched
a cross-collection comparison note that reports agreement and disagreement between strata without averaging them

failure_taxonomy.borrowed_from: the deployment's own grading vocabulary, extended for synthesis

classes.meaning: All required evidence items present, all citations resolve and support.
Answer is accurate as far as it goes but omits one or more required evidence items. THE CENTRAL FAILURE CLASS OF THIS STUDY. Must never be scored as correct.
One or more required documents never appeared in the retrieved sources. Distinguishes a retrieval failure from a generation failure -- the answer could not have been complete.
Answer content is correct but one or more cited chunk_ids do not support the claim on resolution. A distinct failure, never a pass.
QueryResponse.truncated is set. Recorded separately; expected to rise with top_k and context_window.
No LLM configured; the response is not an answer. Excluded from scoring, recorded as an infrastructure condition.
429 or 503. Retried with backoff, counted in the cost vector, never scored as an answer failure.

measures.citation_support: Fraction of cited chunk_ids that, on resolution through GET /v1/chunks, actually support the claim they are attached to.
measures.document_coverage_at_k: Of the distinct doc_ids in a question's gold evidence set, the fraction that appear in the retrieved sources at k. This replaces naive chunk recall as the primary retrieval measure, and is computable from POST /v1/retrieve alone at zero generation cost.
measures.synthesis_completeness: Of the enumerated required evidence items for a question, the fraction the returned answer actually states, with each stated item's citation resolving to a supporting chunk in the correct source document.
measures.yield: credited datapoints per billable call, where billable_calls = provider_calls + llm_calls. Null when no cost record exists -- never the raw count.

open_questions.impact: Determines whether the leaderboard measures correctness or self-consistency.
open_questions.question: Is there an existing ASM question set with reference answers, or should the run generate a synthesis-anchored set from the corpus?

open_questions.default_if_unanswered: treat all readable ASM collections as equally important; if the call budget binds, order by descending document count
open_questions.question: Are all readable ASM collections equally important, or is one primary?

open_questions.resolved_value: Majority multi-paper synthesis within a single collection; minority single-document lookup retained as a control class.
open_questions.status: RESOLVED by operator directive 'preferable multi-paper synthesis'

open_questions.default_if_unanswered: the Creator declares an explicit per-collection billable-call ceiling in its workflow and reports bound_hit if reached
open_questions.impact: A per-collection design multiplies call volume by the number of strata, and the synthesis-favouring structures are themselves multi-call. The two multiply.
open_questions.question: Is there a call or spend ceiling for this study?

content.revision_note: Revision 2. Supersedes context_e3d42147e03b0923f9a600d797f1045d5a2661ec8abd3043d585d46e9ef09696. Incorporates two operator rulings: collections are measured separately with no union arm, and the benchmark is weighted toward multi-paper synthesis. The rank-2 benchmark form was rewritten from single-chunk anchoring to multi-document evidence sets; the primary retrieval measure was changed from chunk recall to document coverage; incomplete_synthesis was added as the central failure class.

phases.note: Findings must be allowed to strike axes from the plan. Per collection, resolve size, graph availability, and readable status. A sweep designed before the tenant has been inspected is not acceptable.
Per collection. Frozen before any scored trial.
Per collection, through POST /v1/retrieve on document_coverage_at_k. No configuration reaches a paid generation trial without passing here.
Per collection. One axis changed per trial from a named prior configuration; a multi-axis change is recorded as exploratory and is not evidence for any single axis.
Per collection. Compare single_shot against the synthesis-oriented structures on the winning parameter configuration.
Per-collection findings, then the cross-collection comparison that reports agreement without averaging.
